# Working of Bucket Sort

#### Course: DSA with C++

## Working of Bucket Sort

1. Scatter

First, we divide the vector into smaller buckets. The number of buckets and the range of a bucket depends on the data in the vector.

Since our sample vector contains numbers from 1 to 14, it's easier to divide the elements into 3 buckets (0-5, 5-10, 10-15).

![3 Buckets With Certain Range](data:image/png;base64,)

Now, let's insert the elements in their respective buckets.

![Insert Elements to Respective Buckets](data:image/png;base64,)

Each bucket has some unsorted elements. Sorting these elements will be our next step.

But first, you need to learn an important detail about the scattering process.

Scattered Elements Must Be Distributed Uniformly

Consider a different vector {5, 7, 1, 12, 15}. You might be tempted to scatter the elements in the following way:

- Bucket 1: To contain elements from 0-13 (i.e. 5, 7, 1, 12).
- Bucket 2: To contain elements from 14-28 (i.e. 15).

But this would be ineffective as the elements aren't uniformly distributed across the buckets.

A better option would be to use Bucket 1 for elements from 0-7 (1, 5, 7) and Bucket 2 for elements from 8-16 (12, 15).

Now, we'll go back to sorting our sample vector, but only after you've taken a short quiz!
